slides.0.title: Armagnac Regions and Style
slides.0.subtitle: Bas-Armagnac, Ténarèze, Haut-Armagnac and the character of column distillation
slides.1.title: The three districts
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Bas-Armagnac
slides.1.highlights.0.content: West: poor, acidic clay loam with iron (reddish-brown) and silty boulbènes; Baco suits the sandy soils; light, fruity and delicate spirits; about 62% of output (armagnac.fr, Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Armagnac-Ténarèze
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Centre: a transitional zone with boulbènes and heavy, fertile clay-limestone terreforts; fuller in style, peaking after long ageing; about 37%
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Haut-Armagnac
slides.1.highlights.2.content: South and east: limestone and clay-limestone hills with sparse vineyards; only about 1% (Wikipedia, armagnac.fr)
slides.1.content: The 1909 Fallières Decree named the three districts; AOC status followed in 1936.
slides.2.title: Contrast with Cognac
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Distillation
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Armagnac is traditionally distilled once in a column still at roughly 52–60%; continuous distillation was patented in 1818. Cognac is double-distilled in pot stills
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Scale
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Armagnac makes about 3 million bottles a year against about 220 million for Cognac (Wikipedia figures), mostly from small producers
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Style
slides.2.highlights.2.content: More congeners are kept, giving a sturdier, rustic, dried-fruit character; vintages (Millésime) are common, with a single harvest aged at least 10 years
slides.2.content: Claims about local Gascon oak were not confirmed by our sources and are left out.
slides.3.title: Vintages and milestones
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Key dates
slides.3.highlights.0.content: In 1310 Cardinal Vital du Four wrote of its virtues; 1646 first distillation record; 1818 continuous-still patent; 1909 delimitation; 1936 AOC
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Blanche d'Armagnac
slides.3.highlights.1.content: An unaged white spirit recognised by the AOC since 2005 (see Level 1)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Essay pointers
slides.3.highlights.2.content: When comparing Armagnac with Cognac, contrast soils, varieties (Baco, Folle Blanche), stills and scale
slides.3.content: Sources differ on the XO minimum, so check WSET materials before the exam.
